title: Shaping of the finite-size chaos crossover in Floquet circuits by coherent-mismatch architecture
authors: Xiangjun Tan, Wenqi Liu, Hanjie Zhu, Wenkai Bai, Zhanning Wang
abstract: We study how the spatial profile of a deterministic coherent gate perturbation affects finite-size quasienergy statistics and operator dynamics in U(1)-symmetric XXZ Floquet circuits. Using a shared homogeneous reference, we compare a single modified bond with an alternating perturbation applied across the whole chain. After separating symmetry sectors and checking several known integrable forms, we find that the alternating circuits move toward circular orthogonal ensemble level statistics and change operator-space entanglement and out-of-time-order correlations at smaller local amplitudes than the single defects. For intermediate numbers of modified bonds, the response is nonmonotonic and also depends on where the bonds are placed, so bond density alone is not enough. A perturbative analysis identifies the additive weight of many modified bonds, while coherent spatial interference reshapes the coupling between nearby eigenstates.
summary: This paper analyzes how the spatial pattern of local gate perturbations affects the onset of chaos in Floquet XXZ quantum circuits. By comparing single-defect versus alternating perturbation patterns, the authors show that the placement of defects, not just their total number, dictates the system's approach to random matrix statistics. This highlights the importance of spatial coherence in controlling quantum dynamics.
main_problem: The study investigates how the spatial pattern of a deterministic coherent gate perturbation influences the finite-size chaos crossover and operator dynamics in U(1)-symmetric XXZ Floquet circuits.
main_result: The spatial arrangement of perturbations is crucial; alternating circuits show faster chaotic crossover than single defects, and the response is nonmonotonic, meaning bond density alone is insufficient.
method: The authors use perturbative analysis, comparing different circuit architectures (single-defect vs. alternating full-support) by analyzing bond-averaged generators and spectral statistics.
model_or_system: The system is a one-dimensional Floquet circuit based on the XXZ model, characterized by a conserved U(1) charge. The dynamics are governed by the Floquet operator, which is perturbed by local coherent gates.
key_observables: Finite-size quasienergy statistics (e.g., gap ratios), operator-space entanglement, and out-of-time-order correlations (OTOCs).
important_parameters: The local amplitude of the perturbation ($\delta$), the number of modified bonds ($K$), and the spatial placement of these bonds.
main_assumptions: The analysis often compares the system to known integrable forms and assumes the validity of perturbative expansions for small perturbations.
figures_summary: Figures compare gap ratios for various gate assignments (central vs. alternating full support) and show the evolution of operator distances ($D_{loc}(t)$) when defects are displaced from the center.
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares different circuit architectures (homogeneous, single-defect, alternating full-support) by analyzing their bond-averaged generators, testing for deviations from integrability, and measuring spectral statistics.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses how local perturbations shape the transition to chaos in quantum many-body systems, which is highly relevant for understanding quantum thermalization and scrambling in engineered quantum simulators.
